data.abstract: Advanced monitoring systems that combine PD detection with other methods, such as oil monitoring, increase reliability and provide operators with more accurate health assessments. This article studies the electromagnetic (EM) waves emitted from partial discharges in the ultra-high frequency (UHF) range using a special UHF sensor for integration purposes. Given the complex structure of power transformers, diagnosing partial discharges using UHF methods presents several challenges. This study addresses the impact of the transformer tank and other parameters on the impedance matching, and radiation pattern, aiming to enhance the sensitivity of the studied UHF PD sensor. A practical method for selecting the optimal frequency range for PD detection is proposed to improve the effectiveness of the UHF method and enhance the signal-to-noise ratio using frequency spectrum analysis. The results were validated by correlating the phase-resolved partial discharge (PRPD) patterns obtained through the IEC 60270 method with those from both a commercial sensor and the UHF PD sensor studied in this article. This validation confirms the effectiveness of the proposed approach in improving PD detection in power transformers.

data.abstract: This study comparatively examines the electrical degradation characteristics of MIDEL 7131, a synthetic ester-based eco-friendly insulating oil, against conventional mineral oil through laboratory-scale experiments. While dissolved gas analysis (DGA) is a standard diagnostic tool, most studies focus on in-service or failed transformers, which pose significant time and economic constraints. Furthermore, experimental data on dissolved gas evolution trends specifically under electrical stress for emerging eco-friendly oils remain limited. To address these gaps, a scaled-down experimental system was applied to replicate the internal winding structure of actual transformers, enabling cost-effective and efficient simulation of electrical degradation. The research was conducted in two phases. First, AC dielectric breakdown (BD) tests were performed. Second, electrical stress was applied to MIDEL 7131 impregnated specimens based on the partial discharge inception voltage (PDIV) measured in accordance with IEC 60270. Results showed that MIDEL 7131 exhibited higher breakdown voltages and lower total dissolved combustible gas levels compared to mineral oil. Duval Triangle analysis indicated that degradation initiated in the partial discharge zone and progressed into the low-energy discharge (D1) zone. However, a key finding emerged despite differences in cumulative degradation between samples the gas composition plots remained clustered within the same D1 zone. This suggests that while the Duval triangle is effective for identifying fault types, it has limitations in quantitatively assessing the severity or cumulative intensity of electrical stress. These findings provide a critical technical basis for developing early fault-detection methods and enhancing the reliability assessment of eco-friendly insulating oils in power transformers.

data.abstract: Partial discharge (PD) measurement has been established to detect local defects in the oil/paper insulation. Partial discharges can be measured by either electrical PD measurements according to IEC 60270 or by electromagnetic measurements in the ultra-high frequency range (UHF: 300 MHz -3 GHz). The electromagnetic emissions of PD are recorded using an UHF antenna which is installed into the transformer tank. The importance of PD measurements is reflected in the standard for electrical measurements (IEC 60270). Because of the standard, apparent charge, QIEC, is now an essential factor with regard to determining insulation quality in transformers. To also be an accepted factor for quality testing, UHF technology must be reliable and reproducible to complement electrical PD measurements in FAT and SAT. To achieve this, a standardized calibration procedure is needed that makes UHF measurement results from different systems comparable. Because this calibration procedure is lacking, current UHF technology is not yet used as an acceptance criterion for type or routine testing. However, it shows advantages for acceptance tests and diagnostic purposes, e.g. with regard to the signal/noise ratio and the localization of PD sources The contribution will present two different types of ultra-high frequency (UHF) PD sensors for power transformers and explains the installation process. One is for new transformers using dielectric windows and the other is for retrofit of transformers using drain valves. Also, the contribution will provide a description of the calibration process for electromagnetic UHF PD measurements consisting of two steps: 1) Calibration of the measurement system analogous to the calibration of the electrical PD measurement circuit using a defined reference signal. 2) Calibration of the used UHF sensor using its antenna factor (AF). Furthermore, it will provide a recommendation/strategy on how to place window type UHF sensors at new power transformers. Another important aspect of UHF condition monitoring is the three-dimensional localization of PD sources. A combination of electromagnetic simulations and AI was used to improve the localization of PD sources.

data.abstract: The operational lifespan of cross-linked polyethylene (XLPE) insulated power cables is significantly affected by thermal ageing, which can degrade dielectric properties and compromise system reliability. This paper presents an experimental study on the impact of accelerated thermal ageing on the partial discharge (PD) characteristics of 11 kV XLPE cables. The investigation involved subjecting both healthy and physically worn cables to thermal ageing at 100°C for 120 and 240 hours, followed by PD testing as per IEC 60270 standards. Experimental results demonstrate that healthy cables exhibited a slight increase in PD levels—from 1.048 pC (unaged) to 1.513 pC (240 hours)—remaining within acceptable limits. In contrast, damaged cables showed a sharp escalation in PD magnitude, rising from 3.391 pC to 22.17 pC after 240 hours, exceeding the permissible threshold. These findings highlight the critical role of mechanical integrity and thermal stress in accelerating insulation degradation. The study emphasizes the need for stringent installation practices and regular PD diagnostics in condition-based maintenance. The application of Arrhenius modelling further supports predictive assessment of cable ageing. Future work will focus on evaluating ageing under combined electrical, thermal, and environmental stressors to enhance reliability modelling for HV cable systems. This can be used for advance diagnostics of XLPE cable, predictive maintenance and finally ageing of XLPE cable can be determine.

data.abstract: In power transformers, insulating oil is primarily used to insulate and cool windings and iron cores. When a transformer fails, its high temperature, discharge, and arc phenomenon will cause gas to be generated in the insulating oil. The condition inside the transformer can be analyzed and possible fault types can be diagnosed by analyzing the dissolved gas in the insulating oil. This study proposes a novel method for fault diagnosis based on dissolved gas analysis. The proposed method implements an intelligent fault diagnosis model using an ensemble learning method, which can be used for individual fault assessment of power transformers and on-load tap changers. In the design of the input data of the proposed fault diagnosis model, the percentages of five gases (H2, CH4, C2H6, C2H4, C2H2) are selected. Finally, the normal and fault data from a power company and IEC TC10 document are used to train the proposed model. Subsequently, actual data from a technology company are used for testing. The test results verify the feasibility of the proposed fault diagnosis technology. The accuracy of transformer fault diagnosis exceeds 71 % (seven diagnostic types) and more than 82 % (three diagnostic types); the accuracy of on-load tap changer fault diagnosis achieves 75 % (three diagnostic types).

data.title: The detection and classification of partial discharges in power transformer using the acoustic method

data.abstract: Partial discharges are the main causes of degradation of the insulation system in power transformers. Their permanent monitoring is therefore of fundamental importance, in the way that it ensures a better assessment of the level of electrical insulation. Several types of partial discharges are present in power transformers depending on the components of the electric field to which the insulation is subjected. Many on-line methods are used to the continuous measurement of partial discharges, including the acoustic method which doing both measurement of electrical parameters and localization of the sources of partial discharges. This article deals with both recognition and classification of partial discharges by analysis of acoustic signals. The goal is to reproduce various types of partial discharges present in the transformers (surface, internal, and corona discharges) by several structures of electrodes in a prototype transformer filled with insulating oil. The generation of partial discharges is done using an experimental setup consisting of a controlled 220V/50kV HV transformer connected to a prototype of transformer containing an electrode system. The experimental procedure are carried out according to the protocol of the IEC 61270 standard. The measurement of the acoustic signals on the tank is carried out using a conventional broadband sensor from the company ACOUSTIC EMISSION (GI150). Both signal analysis obtained in the frequency domain using the time-frequency response and high-resolution frequency analysis (MUSIC) makes it possible to clearly distinguish the type of discharge produced.
